source_text.body:
Automate browser workflows in a cloud browser
A user set up Dot in its cloud browser for autonomous workflows, but it often broke down and asked for repeated logins and permissions.
·
Oct 29, 2026
Done with
DO
Dots
What they did
The user tried to set up Dot for autonomous browser work in its cloud browser, including saving site credentials and granting permissions so it could handle tasks without supervision. In practice, they still had to babysit it: it sometimes could not open links, failed on a PDF download-upload handoff, and would ask them to log in again or reapprove access they had already granted.
How it went
For this user, the workflow saved less time than it consumed because they kept debugging browser failures and repeated auth prompts. Comments said others had better results with different use cases, but this post’s reported outcome was mostly frustration rather than usable automation.
Worth knowing
A practical catch was file handling: when Dot downloaded something, the user said it sometimes sent the file to them and then asked them to upload it back into the same chat.
Try it yourself
with
Dots
Copy prompt
Using your cloud browser, run this workflow for me: [describe the steps, such as logging into a site, exporting a report, and filling a spreadsheet]. Tell me up front which logins or permissions you need so I can grant them all at once, then carry out the task and report what you did. Pause and show me before you submit any form, send anything, or delete anything.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/OpenAI/comments/1x54240/i_spend_more_time_babysitting_my_dot_than_i
